Thresholds and duties differ, and the marketplace is cross-border by default.' | Owner: User | Deferred To: /create-prd-security — which is exactly the stage meta/constraints.md:364 assigns the empirical legal work to ('The US instrument NAMES are deferred to /create-prd-security ... No ideation source contains them, and this pipeline will not assert them'). 01.08:43 additionally routes the numeric threshold there. The Dimension-4 framing also misreads the file: :10 is Overview rationale ('Under EU/UK consumer law the distinction decides...'), not a normative rule, and :29 explicitly disclaims ownership of exactly the content cited as contradictory — 'It does not own: consumer rights mechanics (returns, withdrawal windows, warranties), which belong to 13/14/05, or tax/VAT treatment'. The only normative publication list at :25 is jurisdiction-neutral ('legal name, geographic address, contact details, and (where applicable) a company or VAT number' — 'where applicable' is the hedge), and the buyer-facing disclosure copy at :19 is 'this seller is a private individual; consumer protections do not apply', which names no 14-day right. All three quotes exist (identity-profiles-organizations-cx.md:305, :314; 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:114; 01.02.02-organization-creation-lifecycle.md:163), but this is a terminology clash, not two normative statements that cannot both hold. 01.03.01:114's 'the org is frozen, not broken' contrasts frozen with BROKEN in a States/what-user-sees row — its operative content is 'Read paths continue working' and a banner; it states no rule about booking acceptance. The same file uses the CX sense one screen earlier: 01.03.01:72 — 'short enough that the org is not frozen through a release cycle'. So 01.03.01 does not take a side against CX-16; it is loose prose in the same direction. The behavioural rule is stated once, in the file whose job is this cross-cut, and echoed by the owning lifecycle file: CX-16 §5 ('the org must still accept it; who settles it waits on succession ... it closes the gap CX-09 §5 flagged') and 01.02.02:163 ('It is not frozen — other people's bookings depend on it'). Fail-closed (01.03.03:112 D-05) is not violated: 'accept' here is the org not rejecting an inbound request while settlement authority waits on succession — no actor exercises elevated authority, which is precisely what CX-16 §2 describes ('the org keeps operating unadministrable'). Refuted at blocking severity; nothing is invented.

The line reads 'Notification fan-out: Type addition notifies members (their org gained a capability) `[PENDING — Step 5]`' — the behaviour is ASSERTED in the same sentence as the marker. The finding's stated invention is 'Whether adding a type to an existing org notifies its members', and the file answers exactly that: it does. The residual marker covers unstated detail (channel, copy, timing), which is downstream of the vision layer. :80's 'Medium confidence — 1, 3, 5 deferred to Step 5' does not touch fan-out (that is item 4, which is answered). Compare the genuinely open one in the same file at :34, which asks a real question ('could a member be mandated for only the shop and not the venue?') and IS live-tracked — 01.02.01-organization-types-attributes.md:164 Q-04 re-targeted 2026-07-23 to /create-prd-security via 01.03.03 Q-02. Quotes verified (01.02.01-organization-types-attributes.md:82 and D-14:155; meta/constraints.md:267), but the same file carries this exact gap as a live, owned question fifteen lines below the decision the finding says it violates. 01.02.01:163 Q-03 — 'RESOLVED for `constrained` authority → D-14 ... Still open for `floored` authority (DT-10): the statutory returns floor is a property of the *buyer's* jurisdiction, not the record's address, so it does not resolve against the place-record regime profile D-14 uses, and no source states which floors apply.' | Owner: User | Deferred To: '/create-prd-security, with 13/14'. That is a precise statement of why D-14 does NOT govern the :82 row (D-14 is scoped to `constrained` authority resolved against a place-record regime profile; returns floor is `floored` authority keyed to the buyer's jurisdiction), so the 'reproduces the silent-default failure D-14 forbids' framing does not hold — the file distinguishes the two authorities and tracks the open one. The :82 copy is illustrative of the `floored` mechanism, and the row's own text defers the value ('the statutory floor for the buyer's jurisdiction'), naming no jurisdiction as fixed.

All quotes verified (01.02.02-organization-creation-lifecycle.md:84, :163, D-16:257; 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:72, :114, D-14:173; identity-profiles-organizations-cx.md:305), but the two names are two axes of one condition, and the tree states the relation explicitly: 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:111 D-04 — 'Every org must retain at least one full mandate holder | Enforced at departure (01.03.01) and creation (01.02.02); an ownerless org is unadministrable' — echoed at 01.03.01:71 ('an ownerless org is unadministrable (01.03.03 D-04)'). `ownerless` is the party's ownership-axis value (01.02.02:84); `unadministrable` is the consequence for acting. The succession paths are also sequenced, contrary to the claim: 01.03.01:72 runs the offer to the longest-tenured confirmed member with a 14-day contest and then states 'No remaining members → the party stays unadministrable and exits to 01.10 (estates)', while 01.02.02:163 names the same two outward routes ('succession routes via 01.10 (estate) and 01.05.03 (transfer)') — 01.05.03 being the transfer machinery the offer vests through, 01.10 the no-members case. D-14:173's narrowing ('(a) single-member orgs, (b) every non-band org type ... (c) the uncapped owning mandate') is consistent with that, not opposed to it. What is left — one enum or two, which name is canonical — is a representation question for the data model, i.e. downstream of vision.

Verified verbatim on both sides, with no marker on either: 01.05.01-shadow-party-creation-invitation.md:43 — 'Name | Yes | 1–120 characters, counted and compared after the name is normalized' — reinforced at D-09:210 ('a name (≤120 chars, no URLs, no markup)'), against 01.01.02-artist-names-aliases-projects.md:36 — 'Display name | 1–100 characters, full Unicode'. The conversion between them is specified as mandatory, twice: 01.05.01:53 ('the name on a shadow party is alias-shaped: on claim it becomes an alias of a person (01.01.02)') and D-13:214 ('Claiming binds it as an alias of a person'). Neither file references the other's bound, and no open question in 01.05-profile-claiming-verification-index.md (Q-01..Q-03) or 01.01-person-identity-roles-index.md (Q-01, Q-03) touches it. So for a 101–120 character shadow name the claim event has no defined outcome and the four available answers (truncate, reject, widen the alias cap, write out of spec) produce different products. Warning rather than blocking: the band is narrow and rare, and the rest of the claim→alias flow is fully specified, so an implementer is not stopped — but the choice is a product one and is currently unmade.

Quotes verified (01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md D-06:97, :51, :52, Role Lens :17, Behavior :25), and the finding is even right that :52's pointer is mis-numbered — but the question it should point at exists, is live, and covers the exact concern: :105 Q-03 — 'Do share links expire or get revoked, given an EPK may carry rates and contact routes?' | Owner: Agent | Deferred To: `/create-prd-security`.
